body:
Four Spheres That Work Together: 1. Geosphere: rock, soil, sand and melted rock deep below; hydrosphere: all of Earth's water; atmosphere: the layer of air around Earth; biosphere: every living thing. 2. Wind picks up sand that hits rock again and again and wears it into new shapes (weathering). 3. Roots grow into cracks and split rocks apart; roots also hold soil in place so less washes away. 4. Weathering is the wearing away or breaking of rock in place; erosion is moving rock and soil from one place to another. 5. Example: rain (hydrosphere) falls on the bare hill (geosphere) and carries soil downhill (erosion); with no plants (biosphere) to hold it, more soil is lost. 6. Cause and effect: each paragraph tells how one sphere causes a change in another, for example wind causes weathering, water freezing causes cracks to widen.
Erosion on a Hill: A testable hypothesis gives a reason (for example, a steeper hill will lose more soil because the water runs faster). A fair test changes only the height and keeps the soil, the amount of water and the pouring the same, with more than one trial at each height. Data are in centimeters and grams. Typical results: soil washed off goes up as the height goes up, so the graphed points rise from left to right. Grass would hold the soil and reduce the loss. Spheres: the hydrosphere (water) erodes the geosphere (soil); plants would add the biosphere.
Earth's Systems Check: 1. The atmosphere: ash shot into the sky, blocked sunlight, made towns dark at noon and made the air cooler. 2. Hot rock and gas melted the snow; the meltwater mixed with ash and soil to make mudflows that rushed into rivers, turned them brown and made them flood. 3. Harmed: the forest was knocked flat and buried, and many plants died. Helped: the ash broke down into mineral-rich soil, and new plants grew, then insects, birds and deer returned. 4. Example: hot rock from the volcano (geosphere) melted the snow (hydrosphere), and the mudflows buried the forest (biosphere). 5. Sand, mud and ash carried by water: "a layer of sediment, the sand, mud and ash carried by the water." 6. Yes: atmosphere (ash cloud blocked sunlight and cooled the air), geosphere (hot rock poured down; ash became new soil), hydrosphere (snow melted; rivers flooded), biosphere (forest buried; plants and animals returned).
Scoring tip: on question 4, a chain that names three spheres but does not show how each event causes the next is Developing on reasoning.
title: Answer key: Earth's Systems
